# The thin-edge obstruction stays above 1/e on its certified active branch

This is a diagnostic for the proposed universal individual-capacity floor 1/e. It does not prove that floor for arbitrary bodies. It proves that the already audited thin-edge obstruction cannot refute it in its certified small-parameter phase, and identifies an exact necessary endpoint of the same zero-outside-coarea vertex-cap branch. Beyond that endpoint the old formulas cannot be extrapolated.

We use the exact actual family and notation of `candidate e52160c774656005`: d=4, middle regular simplex T, endpoint fibers D_delta defined by lambda_2+lambda_3+lambda_4 <= delta, relative endpoint mass alpha=4 delta^3-3 delta^4, and outward width h>0. Its all-active-family classification is proved for sufficiently small fixed delta followed by sufficiently small h. No assertion that this classification persists until the phase endpoint below is assumed.

## 1. A normal field giving an exact limiting lower bound

On the zero-outside-coarea vertex branch, the limiting source coordinates are

    y_0=y_1=x,  y_2=y_3=y_4=z,
    2x+3z=1,  256 x z^2(x-z)=alpha,
    1/5 <= x < 1/4.

Write beta=1/B for the common source-facet capture average and theta_J for the total response weight of the two edge-vertex caps. These are

    beta = 256 x^2 z^3 / [1-4(2x^2+3z^2)],
    theta_J = 2x(1-4x) / [1-4(2x^2+3z^2)] >= 0.

Choose the source facet F_0. Its shared endpoint patch A_0=D_delta intersect F_0 is the corner simplex, in the remaining four barycentric coordinates, cut by lambda_2+lambda_3+lambda_4 <= delta. Thus

    area(A_0)/area(F_0)=delta^3.

Use a nonnegative normal-dependent field that is constant one in the physical variable at the normal of F_0 and vanishes at all other facet normals of the three fibers. A continuous nonnegative function of the normal with those values exists because this is a finite set of distinct normals. Its physical dependence is constant, hence globally convex. The truncating facet of D_delta has a distinct normal.

Every actual active edge-cone cap captures one entire endpoint and misses the other. Every actual active complementary-cone cap misses both endpoints. These are exact statements at positive width: zero endpoint strip coarea and connectedness of the endpoint interior force the continuous smoothing integrand to be identically zero or one, including on the closure. Therefore the SUM of the two endpoint boundary profiles is theta_J pointwise on their common copy of D_delta. This statement survives the h-to-zero limit and does not replace closed boundary selectors by interior indicators.

The limiting efficiency of the displayed field is consequently

    R(delta) = [beta + theta_J delta^3]/[1+2 delta^3].       (1)

The convergence is uniform over all actual menus in the certified small-delta phase, by the all-menu convergence in the primary source. In particular the supremal field efficiency for ANY such menu is at least R(delta)-o_delta(1) as h tends to zero. The lower bound applies even before optimizing the menu.

## 2. An exact rational floor above 1/e

Put t=x/z, so 1 <= t < 3/2. Then

    beta = 256 t^2 / [(2t+3)^3(-4t^2+12t-3)].

The denominator is positive in this interval. The polynomial identity

    625 t^2 - (2t+3)^3(-4t^2+12t-3)
      = (t-1)^2(32t^3+112t^2+81)

proves beta >= Gamma_4=256/625 without invoking a separate simplex inequality.

The branch in which every low-vertex cap misses D_delta necessarily satisfies delta <= 1-4x; Section3 proves this directly. In particular delta <= 1/5. Since theta_J is nonnegative, (1) gives

    R(delta) >= Gamma_4/(1+2/125) = 256/635 > 3/8 > 1/e.   (2)

The last comparison is elementary: 8*256 > 3*635, and the first four terms of the exponential series give e > 1+1+1/2+1/6=8/3. Thus no decimal approximation enters (2).

In the rigorously certified sufficiently small fixed-delta phase, choose h small enough that the uniform convergence loss is smaller than half the positive gap 256/635-3/8. Every actual menu then admits the displayed field with efficiency strictly above 3/8, hence strictly above 1/e. The individual Gamma_4 obstruction is therefore compatible with a 1/e floor in its entire currently proved regime.

## 3. The exact geometric endpoint of the old branch

For a vertex-i simplex cap whose proper cut section has centroid y, its affine cap margin can be normalized as

    f_i(lambda)=1-sum_{k != i} lambda_k/(4y_k),

with the retained cap f_i >= 0. For a low index i in {2,3,4}, maximize this margin over D_delta. Because x >= z, its maximum is attained with lambda_i=delta, all other low coordinates zero, and the remaining mass on the two high coordinates. The result is

    max_{D_delta} f_i = 1-(1-delta)/(4x).                 (3)

Since the two endpoint bodies coincide, two endpoint caps with opposite base shifts can both miss their interiors only if max f_i <= 0. Conversely, if the inequality is strict, base tilt zero misses both with a margin. Hence the exact necessary and sufficient geometric condition for a zero-cost pair of these fixed low-vertex caps is

    delta <= 1-4x.                                     (4)

At equality the first touching point is on D_delta's exposed low-vertex face. For larger delta the region f_i>0 in D_delta has positive four-dimensional volume; no pair of opposite integer shifts can miss both endpoints. The old outside-mass-zero and outside-coarea-zero argument is therefore unavailable. At positive width the strict inequality in (4) supplies the required reserve, while the exact limiting equality is the transition point of this candidate branch.

Combine equality in (4), x=(1-delta)/4, z=(1+delta)/6, with the old common-cap equation. One obtains

    P(delta)=101 delta^4-92 delta^3-24 delta^2-16 delta+4=0. (5)

There is exactly one root delta_* in (0,1/5). Indeed P(0)=4, P(1/5)=-459/625, and throughout [0,1/5],

    P'(delta)=404 delta^3-276 delta^2-48 delta-16
              <=404/125-16 <0.

The approximate value 0.177164169 is only descriptive and not used in any proof. The old branch itself is unique as long as 1 <= t <=3/2: its common-cap equation is

    alpha=256t(t-1)/(2t+3)^4,

whose derivative has the sign of -4t^2+12t-3, positive on this interval. As delta grows, x therefore increases and 1-4x decreases. Consequently equality (5) is the unique point at which (4) fails along this algebraic branch.

This is a necessary endpoint of the certified mechanism, not a proof that no competing active normal appears earlier. A valid continuation past delta_* must reclassify actual active directions, retain positive endpoint strip coareas, and recompute the full response weights and kernel-centroid equations. Substituting larger delta into (1) or the old source equation would not answer the 1/e question for the actual mixed body.

## 4. Remaining scope

The small-parameter obstruction, and its audited odd-integer product with no globally heavy fiber, both stay strictly above 1/e by the same field lower bound. A universal 1/e capacity floor is still unproved and unrefuted by these results. The exact phase transition explains why increasing the endpoint volume in the old formulas is not a valid route to a stronger obstruction.
